headline: US loses measles elimination status
pages: A committee of the Pan American Health Organization said Tuesday that the United States no longer has measles elimination status, a finding STAT described as largely symbolic. STAT reported that the country has recorded more than 5,000 measles cases this year, the first time the count has passed 5,000 since 1991. About 96 percent of infections were in people who were unvaccinated or whose status was unknown. State data show 10 measles deaths this year, while the CDC's website lists six. Elimination status means the disease is no longer spreading continuously within a country. Losing it matters because it signals weaker vaccination coverage and could make future outbreaks harder to contain.
